changes: Scribe 'vipravaro' kept, but confidence lowered to low: in the verse it most likely means 'an excellent brahmin' (vipra-vara), not a personal name; added 'vipra' (brahmin) as a title.

Tithi changed from ekādaśī to caturdaśī (probable). 'Śambhos tithi' names the tithi whose deity is Śiva, which is the 14th; kṛṣṇa caturdaśī is Śivarātri. Ekādaśī (Rudra = 11) and aṣṭamī are noted as alternatives.
Year: added a tentative reading of parjanya as Indra = 14, read right to left with bhū 1 and pañca 5 to give ŚS 1451 (≈1529 CE). It is marked as uncertain.
Kept month Jyeṣṭha (śukra), paksa kṛṣṇa (asita) and weekday Sunday (ravau).

date.as_written: bhūpaṃ ca parjanyayuteṣu śāke śukrākhyamāsāsitapakṣake ravau śaṃbhos tithau

notes: 'Vipravaro lilekha' most likely means 'an excellent brahmin wrote [this]', which hides the scribe's name. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Vipravara' takes the epithet as a name, so it is doubtful. The chronogram 'bhūpaṃ ca parjanya-' appears corrupt; the catalogue reads it as bhū-pañca-parjanya. Parjanya is not a standard number word. If it stands for Indra (= 14), reading right to left gives ŚS 1451 = c. 1529 CE. That is only a guess, and other values for parjanya would change the year. Śukra is the old name for Jyeṣṭha. 'Śambhos tithi' is most probably caturdaśī (Śiva's tithi; kṛṣṇa 14 = Śivarātri), but ekādaśī (Rudra = 11) or aṣṭamī cannot be ruled out. The colophon ends Skandha 12, adhyāya 13, and includes a stock blessing for the writer and reader (lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ śubham astu).
